cards.claim: GDT706 C019 extends f86v6.25 locally: from a hot wood-preparation share I, measure hot drug share I and heat it to stage III; the written result bundle is a drug portion led fully to the terminal heating state. The edge is ykaiin#5 → okeeeey#7; or#6 supplies the written drug-portion carrier inside the bundle, not another edge. The live rival is two separate register entries at #6/#7; changed material and operation at ofchedy#8 stop the path, so later qokaiin#9 cannot be reached by skipping it.

evidence.quote:
## Result

The search now has both a complete outer map and a completely read near zone.
Forty-two action windows that were still unbound at the start contain 161 later semantic items. The
nearest 28 rank-2/rank-3 cells divide into one admitted result bundle, ten
useful holds, and seventeen visible stops.

The new local reading is:

> **C019 / f86v6.25#2-7:** Aus dem Anteil I des heißen Holzansatzes einen
> heißen Drogenanteil I abmessen. Den so abgemessenen Drogenanteil I auf Stufe
> III erhitzen. Ergebnis: Die Drogenportion ist vollständig bis zur letzten
> Heizstufe geführt.

This is materially more concrete than a generic action sequence: it names the
source share, measured drug share, heat stage, written result material, and
written terminal heating state.

## Why #6 is not skipped

The new relation's source is `#5 ykaiin`, while its state endpoint is
`#7 okeeeey`. The intervening `#6 or` is not discarded. It supplies the missing
written patient, *Drogenportion*, and remains in the rendered result bundle
`#6-7`. In the cumulative graph it is a hull-only material carrier rather than
an endpoint, because C019 asserts one action-to-result relation, not two
independent relations.

The strongest alternative is that #6 and #7 begin two separate register
entries. That keeps C019 occurrence-bound. The next entry, `#8 ofchedy`
(*fertig getrocknete Blütenmasse*), changes both material and operation and
therefore ends this result path. The later `#9 qokaiin` cannot be selected by
skipping that break.

punctuation or a written patient change; #7 may begin another phase of the
same material.

derived from the broader action `aufbereiten`.

cards.claim: GDT708 A024 retains an object-block hold with state/degree → state/degree → material → terminal product ending at #7. Later oechedy#9 is a tempting finished middle-stage dried-mass reading matching drying and middle degree better, but the first terminal product at #7 and a new quantity/material start at #8 intervene. evidence.quote:

| case | visible order | best end | decision |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A012 | quantity → material → state/degree → terminal product | #6 | C021 |
| A014 | quantity → state/degree → terminal product | #5 | object-block hold |

A043 is the strongest local/formal countercase because explicit #2 `dy`/`;`
places its finished dry portion immediately at #3. It loses to A012 only on

The no-skip first-terminal rule therefore cannot jump to #9.

or action agreement for new graph edges.

cards.claim: GDT708 proposes a variable batch architecture: an action is followed by the shortest coherent batch card, ending at the first terminal material product or the first material, operation or grade reset. An attribute stack may precede the product; this replaces a fixed three-token result description in that working model. A012/C021 is the local product candidate, A014/A024 remain object-block holds, and shorter prefixes remain held at their first overextension. These analytical cuts do not establish written punctuation, participant changes or a portable semantic syntax.

## What changed in the working model

The surviving material is not well described by a fixed three-token result.
The useful form is variable:

> action + shortest coherent batch card, ending at the first terminal
> material product or at the first material, operation or grade reset

| case | visible order | best end | decision |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A012 | quantity → material → state/degree → terminal product | #6 | C021 |
| A014 | quantity → state/degree → terminal product | #5 | object-block hold |
| A024 | state/degree → state/degree → material → terminal product | #7 | object-block hold |

places its finished dry portion immediately at #3. It loses to A012 only on
the exact material-and-degree return needed for a new edge. #4
changes middle degree to grade end and #5 adds grade III. The old immediate
hold therefore survives, while its GDT707 three-item extension is stopped.

## The five shorter paths

A073, A070, A029, A017 and A004 all have the same best cut at two items. Their
third item is the first overextension:

- A073 changes to dry Arzneikompositum and restarts the grade;
- A070 restarts with broad `trocken` after the hot-dry checkpoint;
- A029 adds a new dry, measured, completed middle-stage product;
- A017 contradicts middle degree with cold grade-start;
- A004 changes the just-written middle degree to grade end.

A024 also has a tempting later #9 `oechedy`, “fertige, bis zur Mittelstufe
getrocknete Masse”. It matches drying and middle degree better than #7, but the
first terminal product #7 and the new quantity/material start #8 intervene.
The no-skip first-terminal rule therefore cannot jump to #9.

These are useful practical fragments, but still lack enough material, degree
or action agreement for new graph edges.
